items.raw_snippet: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews, 2025, 27(02), 2035-2076 Publication history: Received on 18 July 2025; revised on 24 August 2025; accepted on 26 August 2025 Article DOI: https://doi.org/10.30574/wjarr.2025.27.2.3057 Abstract Background: Artificial intelligence integration in due diligence procedures of mega-large merger acquisition dealings has been brought out as a powerful method in the American business world. Advanced analytics and machine learning algorithms have proven to hold a lot of promise in terms of improving the accuracy of the evaluation of transactions, and also in terms of mitigating time pressures that are normally promulgated in view of intricate MandA assessments. We have applied the machine learning algorithms based on AdaBoost and support vector machine models as a predictive analysis. Results: Analysis indicated that AI-based due diligence platforms have a prediction accuracy of 80.1% in the determination of merger success when compared to traditional approaches, which had 62.7% accuracy.

items.title: Federal AI Projects Get Priority in TMF Funding Dash
items.snippet: The U.S. federal Technology Modernization Fund is racing to push new money into ...
items.raw_snippet: The U.S. federal Technology Modernization Fund is racing to push new money into generative artificial intelligence and permitting projects across the federal government before its authority to make new investments expires at the end of September. TMF Acting Executive Director Jessie Posilkin announced Thursday that the fund is prioritizing two new calls for proposals: one focused on "the fast and responsible adoption of generative AI" and another on faster permitting technology. She described the effort as building on the fund's earlier investments in cloud, security and automation. The speed tracking for GenAI projects comes amid a reauthorization cliff that has hung over the TMF for months, with Congress allowing TMF's authorization to lapse in December for the first time since the fund's 2017 creation. The AI call for proposals was developed in collaboration with General Services Administration's USAi team and aims to fund projects that prepare agency data and infrastructure for AI, pilots emerging AI applications or deploys secure enterprise-scale AI capabilities.
